did: Designed TAKES4: first as home filing GitHub issues with an App, then, on the owner's path A decision, reshaped into takes brought to a session by a pasted block with a derived take ID, home finding "Became #n" by public GitHub search with no key, takes found again by status, sort and search, and Part E retired with a cutover; filed asks #3199–#3201 (answered, then superseded) and drove #3209 through ten fresh-context review rounds to merge.

calls.title: C585: the owner's four statuses ride the conveyor's stations
options: a new status column beside the conveyor
the conveyor retired for a status of its own
calls.why: Every conveyor invariant holds unchanged and the owner sees one status per take; Bring is the only move to Brought, and home's found issue is the move to Became.
calls.undo: Give the statuses a table of their own and restore the station words.

calls.title: C586: the take ID and the block
options: a derived ten-character ID and this block
calls.why: One word to GitHub search, computed alike on phone and home, nothing stored.
calls.undo: Change the ID function and the block module.

calls.title: C587: how home finds Became #n
options: two searches of the owner's own items every 15 minutes
calls.why: One bounded request pair a pass, and no stranger can link a take.
calls.undo: Change the query or interval in the search pass.

calls.title: C589: the status words
options: show the pull request working on it
hide closed issues' takes under a fold
calls.why: In the owner's terms, with only what home can know.

left: docs/takes-to-sessions.md states its limits: a removed line or a repo gone private freezes an item's last-seen state, private repos are never seen, more than a page leaving during one stop of the first pass is outside the design
